key_insight: Self Gradient Forcing extends self-forcing video diffusion so earlier generated frames are not just reused as frozen history, but can be adjusted by future losses through the key-value cache. This makes long-video extrapolation more trainable and better aligned with future generation needs.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a limitation in autoregressive video diffusion: self-forcing reduces exposure bias, but the historical KV cache remains a fixed rollout state, so later frames cannot improve how earlier latents are written into keys and values for long-range video generation.
method: Train on self-generated histories rather than ground-truth contexts, following the self-forcing paradigm.
Allow future-frame losses to backpropagate into the representation of earlier generated latents through the cache-writing process.
Optimize the model so cached keys and values become more useful for long-video extrapolation instead of being treated as immutable rollout memory.
impact: For practitioners building long-video generative models, this can improve temporal consistency and long-horizon quality by making the model learn from its own future consequences. It is especially relevant for reducing drift and improving extrapolation beyond short training windows.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing ground-truth conditioning vs self-forcing vs self gradient forcing.
An annotated KV-cache flow graphic highlighting frozen cache state versus gradient-updated cache writing.
A before/after timeline of generated video frames illustrating long-range drift reduction.
An icon-based comparison chart for exposure bias, rollout memory, and future-loss supervision.
paper_title: Self Gradient Forcing: Native Long Video Extrapolation
paper_authors: Junhao Zhuang, Shiyi Zhang, Yuxuan Bian, Yaowei Li, Yawen Luo
